newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open at historic highs.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open at historic highs.

text.p: French stocks opened at historic highs on Monday, buoyed by the strong performance of the dollar and bond markets, brokers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 7.49 points, or 0.31 percent, at 2,432.59 at 0920 GMT. It opened at 2,426.82, exceeding the peak of 2,426.13 points reached on Friday.
The CAC-40 January futures contract was up eight points at 2,437.
Volume was 970 million francs in the first half hour of trading.
Shares in appliance maker Moulinex fell on the company's announcement on Friday that it would raise 525 million francs of capital by issuing 5,646,191 shares priced at 93 francs each.

Its shares were down 2.33 percent at 126 francs after partially recovering from an early low of 122.10 francs on Moulinex's forecast, included in the prospectus, of an improvement in its operating result for 1996/97.

Shares in bank Credit Foncier were down 0.95 percent at 62.50 francs. Angry employees have been holding top executives hostage at the headquarters since Friday to protest against the government's plans for the bank.

Energy majors rose on the gains in the dollar, which was trading at 5.4714/24 francs, up from 5.4550 on Friday. Total was 1.05 percent higher at 451.70 francs. Elf-Aquitaine gained 0.78 percent to 514 francs.

Elf Chairman Philippe Jaffre said in an interview with the Financial Times that Elf may seek acquisitions to reinforce its chemicals unit Elf Atochem. He also reiterated its willingness to reduce its stake in pharmaceuticals unit Sanofi.
